sentence: This project builds a robot system that moves a lightweight imaging camera around a patient's body to take images that fit the patient's anatomy.
This project studies how the human embryo shapes its early form, using stem cell models and optogenetic tools to change signaling patterns.
This project keeps and shares mutant mouse strains, embryonic stem cells and other materials so researchers can study mouse models of human disease.
This project studies how receptors that recognize ligands control signaling inside cells, including the regulation of cardiac function.
This project studies how arginine metabolism changes immune cell function and drives lung cancer in women.
This project studies whether short sleep duration and irregular sleep are linked to vascular inflammation and visceral adiposity, using imaging.
This project builds a computational method to describe how brain networks influence each other over time, and tests it in patients.
This project uses neuroimaging and machine learning to study how subcortical areas respond to sound, and explores non-invasive neuromodulation for disorders of consciousness.
This project tests whether a cancer target can be treated with single domain antibodies called nanobodies and with mRNA that encodes them.
This project pools neuroimaging and genetics datasets from around the world to learn about the neurobiology of Tourette Syndrome and find biomarkers.
This project studies why people do not take part in lung cancer screening, especially in minority populations.
This project builds a 3D dynamic MRI method to measure how the airway collapses during sleep in obstructive sleep apnea.
This project studies how neighborhood, family and child factors predict sleep health in young children living with limited resources.
This project tests multi-omics risk scores for type 2 diabetes in patients with major depressive disorder, using health system biobanks.
This project studies how mutations in enhancers, which act as switches for gene activity, cause limb malformations, using genetically engineered mice.
This project provides tools and consultation so researchers can carry out mental health assessments of children and adolescents.
This project studies how manganese causes neurotoxicity through raised kinase activity in microglia.
This project provides data management, biostatistics and bioinformatics support for a group of related research projects.
This project studies how changing bile acid changes the absorption of different fatty acids and how this relates to fatty liver disease.
This project tries to predict the position and movement of the hand and fingers from muscle signals recorded by implanted electrodes.
